source_title: Pilot-scale optimization of a physical-chemical biogas upgrading system based on a high alkalinity absorbent at ambient pressure and temperature
authors: Edwin G. Hoyos; Saeed Rasekhi; Rogelio Mazaeda; Raúl Muñoz
evidence_class: Primary pilot-scale experimental literature; product-gas measurements
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), article PDF license statement
measurement_basis: Absorption/desorption system with 7.2 L working volume in each column, controlled at 20 °C. Synthetic inlet gas was 65% CH4, 34.5% CO2 and 0.5% H2S. Reported optimum: 90 L/d biogas, 1500 L/d air, L/G 0.7, initial pH 9.5, inorganic carbon 8000 mg C/L, EDTA-Fe 0 mM. Product-gas composition is reported as mean ± standard deviation for 3 weeks of continuous operation.
uncertainty: The article reports composition ± values; methods state steady-state results as mean and standard deviation. The abstract does not state the number of gas-composition observations in the 3-week mean. H2S is reported as not detected without a detection limit.
conversion_and_scaling: No value conversion or scale-up performed. Flow settings remain L/d for this 7.2 L pilot; no energy, chemical consumption per unit gas, capital or commercial-scale coefficient is inferred.
applicability: Reference dataset for carbonate absorption/air stripping as an additional biogas-upgrading technology option in other project contexts; not representative of GreenHub's existing commercial routes.
limitations: Early-stage pilot operated with synthetic gas at a small 7.2 L working volume per column.
No calculation-ready normalized energy or utility demand was transcribed.
The H2S non-detect has no reported analytical detection limit in the abstract.
Product-gas composition is not a methane recovery fraction or a guaranteed commercial specification.
No GreenHub runtime mapping, default, TEA factor or LCA factor is created.
license_note: CC BY 4.0. Attribute the article and preserve its stated units, condition set and scale limitations.
